Review this change for security vulnerabilities.

Changed files (you may Read these and any other file in the repo):
  - supabase/migrations/20260724090000_item_texture.sql

Unified diff (only + lines are new):

=== DIFF: supabase/migrations/20260724090000_item_texture.sql ===
@@ -0,0 +1,6 @@
+-- Knit structure / surface finish — a dimension `material` cannot express.
+-- A ribbed merino knit and a flat merino shirt share a material and differ in
+-- both warmth and formality; without this column that difference was lost at
+-- capture time and unrecoverable afterwards.
+-- Nullable: every existing row predates the field and is backfilled separately.
+alter table public.items add column if not exists texture text;


Investigate per the method in your instructions, then return the findings list.

1	-- items: one row per wardrobe piece. Categories match the prototype + closet filters.
2	create table public.items (
3	  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
4	  user_id     uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
5	  image_url   text not null,                 -- original (storage path)
6	  cutout_url  text,                           -- background-removed (storage path)
7	  name        text,                           -- e.g. "Brushed Oxford" (user-editable)
8	  brand       text,
9	  category    text not null check (category in ('Tops','Bottoms','Outerwear','Shoes','Accessories')),

16	  price       numeric,                         -- enables cost-per-wear later
17	  archived    boolean default false,
18	  created_at  timestamptz default now()
19	);
20	create index items_user_idx on public.items (user_id) where not archived;
21	
22	alter table public.items enable row level security;
23	
24	create policy "items_all_own"
25	  on public.items for all
26	  to authenticated
27	  using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)
28	  with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
29

31	insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public)
32	  values ('wardrobe', 'wardrobe', false)
33	  on conflict (id) do nothing;
34	
35	create policy "wardrobe_rw_own"
36	  on storage.objects for all
37	  to authenticated
38	  using (bucket_id = 'wardrobe' and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select auth.uid())::text)
39	  with check (bucket_id = 'wardrobe' and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select auth.uid())::text);

content.text: The migration only adds a nullable `text` column to `public.items` with `if not exists`. It doesn't drop any constraint/FK/trigger, doesn't touch RLS, doesn't add a default, and introduces no new sink or entry point. RLS on `items` (from `20260615114702_items.sql`) continues to gate the new column via `auth.uid() = user_id`. No security-relevant impact.
